contests.title: Measure 26-267 — Amends Charter: Portland residents decide 2% of city's annual discretionary budget.

big_picture.text: Would amend the Portland Charter to require a participatory budgeting program in which residents propose and select eligible city projects, with a recurring funding floor tied to city discretionary operating expenses.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review

yes.text: Require Portland to establish the resident-participatory process and allocate an amount equivalent to at least 2% of adopted General Fund discretionary ongoing expenses to it, with implementation starting in July 2027.
yes.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review

no.text: The proposed Charter requirement would not be enacted. Existing mayor, administration, council and public-hearing budget processes would continue unless changed by other action.
no.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review

supporters_why.text: Supporters argue that residents should make binding choices about a portion of city spending and point to neighborhood projects chosen through participatory budgeting elsewhere.
supporters_why.qualifier: Attributed published argument where available; otherwise a possible pro-rationale, not an assertion of supporters' private motives.

critics_why.text: Opponents argue that a recurring Charter-mandated amount, without a dedicated new revenue source, would compete with existing services and make the city budget less flexible.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed published argument where available; otherwise an analytical concern, not an invented opposition group.

who_affected.text: People and services within City of Portland may be affected. Exact property/voter eligibility must be checked on the official personalized ballot.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review

money.text: The ballot summary estimates $16.4 million in FY 2027–28 and $17.0 million in FY 2028–29. These are preliminary allocations under a 2% funding-floor formula, not guaranteed new taxes.
money.qualifier: Financial figures are estimates from the original source and are NOT an independently replicated forecast.

other_impacts.text: A formula-based funding commitment can constrain later budget flexibility and requires administration; its benefit compared with a pilot has not been established.
other_impacts.qualifier: Potential secondary effects, not guaranteed outcomes.

one_to_remember.text: The 2% refers to an identified General Fund discretionary-ongoing expense base, not simply 2% of every city expenditure; the text says Council may draw from the overall city budget to satisfy the funding obligation. Resident proposals must still pass feasibility review before binding selection.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review

unresolved.text: Exact implementation costs, approved project criteria, tradeoffs with other programs and final spending depend on subsequent Council decisions. No independent budget reconstruction completed.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared explanation; not a completed independent legal or fiscal review
